title: Maximum Units on a Truck
summary: Given a 2D array boxTypes where each element boxTypes[i] contains the number of boxes of type i and the number of units in each box of type i, and an integer truckSize representing the maximum number of boxes that can be loaded onto the truck, select the boxes to maximize the total number of units loaded, ensuring that the total number of boxes does not exceed truckSize.
statement: Given a 2D array boxTypes where each element boxTypes[i] contains the number of boxes of type i and the number of units in each box of type i, and an integer truckSize representing the maximum number of boxes that can be loaded onto the truck, select the boxes to maximize the total number of units loaded, ensuring that the total number of boxes does not exceed truckSize.
constraints: Each type gives [available boxes, units per box]; load at most truck_size boxes.
hints: Every box uses one capacity slot, so higher units always dominate lower units.
Sort types by units descending and take as many as capacity allows.
For each type load min(count,remaining), add loaded*units, and stop at zero capacity.
Exchanging a loaded lower-unit box for an available higher-unit box improves the total, proving greedy order.
editorial: Exchanging a loaded lower-unit box for an available higher-unit box improves the total, proving greedy order.

tests.explanation: Load one three-unit box, two two-unit boxes, and one one-unit box for eight.
Taking boxes from highest unit values first yields ninety-one.
